response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack software engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and tooling skills, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect for AI accelerators. There is no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, RTL or microarchitecture work, hardware-software co-design, GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture, or deep neural network training/inference optimization. The closest adjacent experience is low-latency service work in DLang, some C/C++ at National Instruments, and embedded/robotics exposure — all far removed from AI accelerator performance architecture. Education (BS Computer Science) meets the 8+ years bar in principle, but the technical domain mismatch is disqualifying for a principal-level IC role in this specialty.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience, including staff-level roles
Some systems/low-level exposure: C/C++ at National Instruments, low-latency DLang microservices
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD) plus open-source and teaching/community leadership
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, microarchitecture, or hardware-software co-design experience
No AI/deep-learning workload, GPU, or SIMD/MIMD architecture background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not hardware performance architecture at principal level

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI accelerator / DNN workload optimization background
Extensive general software engineering seniority and systems-level C/C++ exposure
